YOUR BUSINESS, CLEARLY EXPLAINED

What does web development include?

Web development turns website plans, content and design into a functioning website. For a business, that includes the pages, navigation, mobile layout, enquiry paths and any agreed connections that help visitors find information and take the next step.

We start with your audience and the job the website needs to do. The scope can cover a new business website or an agreed improvement to an existing site, with content and functionality planned together.

Content with a clear purpose

Explain your services, who they are for and what a visitor should do next. Structure pages around useful answers and accurate business information.

A usable mobile layout

Plan readable text, clear navigation and practical controls for different screen sizes. Check the important visitor journeys during the build.

A useful enquiry path

Make contact, booking or enquiry routes easy to understand. Forms and external booking connections are scoped around the actual destination and the tools you use.

A considered technical foundation

Include descriptive page titles, headings, internal links and appropriate search metadata. Review images, loading behaviour, keyboard use and agreed launch checks.

EXAMPLE BRIEFS FOR PLANNING

Build around the next useful visit.

These are examples of website goals to discuss, rather than completed client projects or promised results.

A service business website

Show the work you offer, the areas you serve, common questions and a clear enquiry route. Help a potential customer decide whether your business fits their needs.

A clearer service-page structure

Give each main service a useful page, with a plain-language explanation, relevant examples and links to related information. Keep the navigation easy to follow.

A booking-focused website

Explain what a visitor can book and what happens next. Link to or integrate a supported booking tool where it fits the scope, including any approval or confirmation steps.

PLAN THE JOURNEY BEFORE THE PAGES

How we approach your website.

Agree on the audience, content, functionality and handover before judging the work only by how a homepage looks.

  1. 01

    Define the audience and purpose

    Identify who visits, what they need to understand and the enquiry, booking or other action the website should support. Agree on the pages and scope.

  2. 02

    Organise content and design

    Gather approved business information, brand assets and images you have permission to use. Review a clear page structure and visual direction before the full build.

  3. 03

    Build and review the journeys

    Develop the agreed pages and connections. Review mobile layouts, navigation, keyboard access, links and any form or booking behaviour included in the scope.

  4. 04

    Agree on launch and handover

    Confirm domain and hosting ownership, deployment access, editing arrangements and ongoing support. Check the agreed release steps before the site goes live.

What to bring to the first conversation

  • Your audience, main services and preferred next step for visitors.
  • Existing website, domain and hosting details, if you have them.
  • Approved logo, brand direction, business information and image permissions.
  • Required forms, booking tools, editing needs and a contact for content approval.

PRACTICAL ANSWERS

Common questions about web development.

Can you improve our existing website?

We can review the current site and identify which changes fit its platform and access arrangements. The scope may be a focused improvement or a new build. Existing content, links, domain ownership and any migration requirements should be considered before changing the site.

Do we need to supply all the content?

Content responsibilities are agreed at the start. You provide or approve business facts, service details, contact information and the rights to any images or brand assets. Writing and content organisation can be included in the scope, with your review before publication.

Will the website work on phones?

Mobile layouts and the main visitor journeys are part of planning and review. We check the agreed pages at different screen sizes, along with navigation and readable content. The precise browser, device and accessibility testing included should be stated in the project scope.

Can the website connect to booking tools or enquiry forms?

Yes, where the chosen platform and supported tools allow it. A form needs a real destination and a clear follow-up process; a booking route needs accurate availability and confirmation rules. Integrations, provider charges and access requirements are confirmed before they are included.

How do SEO, AEO and GEO fit into the website?

Clear service pages, useful answers, descriptive titles, internal links and structured data that matches visible content help explain your offering to people and search systems. Public access and indexing also matter. Rankings and AI citations depend on external systems and cannot be guaranteed by a website build.

Who owns the domain, hosting and website access?

Agree on ownership and billing before launch. The scope should identify who controls the domain and hosting accounts, who can publish changes and how access or content will be handed over. Editing options depend on the platform selected for the website.

What happens after the website launches?

Agree on who updates content, reviews enquiries, maintains connected services and handles support. Ongoing changes, hosting and maintenance can involve separate work or provider charges. The handover should make those responsibilities clear.

What affects the price and delivery time?

The number of pages, content work, design requirements, integrations, editing needs and testing all affect scope. Domain, hosting and other providers may charge separately. We review the brief before quoting and setting a delivery plan; no fixed package price or timeline is published here.
